payload.speaker: Rosa
payload.text: Rosa, night watchman. I walk this square after dark and see everything that moves. Nothing out of place yet, but killers hide in plain sight. Hugo, you said little at Dawn. Speak up, and let's hear from everyone before we vote.

payload.speaker: Hugo
payload.text: Hugo here, old salt. Rosa, Lamplighter, you say you see everything after dark, yet you saw nothing worth naming. I'm quiet because I'm counting heads, and I've seen plenty of ships sink from loud captains. Silas Sawdust, Elsie Anvil, Your Worship Luna, Crumb Tess: who was up before dawn with no good reason? Speak plainly and I'll listen.

payload.speaker: Silas
payload.text: Silas, carpenter. I was alone in my workshop last night, with no witnesses, so I can't prove much. But I build with evidence, not pointed fingers. Hugo, you've asked four of us where we were and offered nothing about yourself. That's a frame with no boards. Rosa's right that we should hear everyone first. *knocks on wood* Let's watch that one closely.

payload.speaker: Elsie
payload.text: Elsie, blacksmith. Hugo, you named four of us and gave no account of yourself. Answer that first. I trust calloused hands, and I don't trust a man who points without lifting anything. Silas has a point. Hugo, where were you last night?

payload.speaker: Tess
payload.text: Tess, baker. I judge folk by how they take their bread, and Hugo, you pointed at four of us without ever saying where you were. That tastes like stale crust to me. Answer Elsie's question before anyone else gets pointed at. Luna, you've said nothing yet. A good mayor shouldn't let the dough sit unkneaded.

payload.text: Luna, your mayor, and I call this square to order! I move that we settle one matter before any vote: Hugo answers Elsie's question plainly. Hugo, where were you last night? Pointing at four neighbours is easy. Standing behind your own words is the test. I'll hold my own account for when the motion is carried.
